name: Build the public Fibel documentation site
description:
Build a real documentation site for the released CLI with @valentinkolb/fibel, following the repository-local Fibel skill. Keep the Go CLI independent from the documentation toolchain: Bun, the pinned Fibel package and the lockfile are used only for the site. Place the site in a clear isolated directory and keep normal CLI builds free of Bun requirements.

Start with one complete English locale rather than partially maintained translations. Cover overview, installation, authentication and secret injection, production versus OT&E, DNS read commands, safe mutation workflow, JSON output and exit codes, troubleshooting, security model and explicit limitations. Every command example must be generated from or checked against released CLI help.

Display a prominent notice on the landing page and in persistent site chrome that this is an unofficial community project, not affiliated with, endorsed by, maintained by or supported by INWX GmbH. Link to the official INWX site for official services and support. Do not use official logos or visual branding in a way that implies affiliation.

Use normal Fibel Markdown content and configuration, retain raw Markdown/llms routes, search, light/dark behavior and the default attribution unless there is a concrete reason to change them. Set a real siteUrl only when the publication hostname is selected; do not invent a production domain. Hosting and DNS rollout are separate from building and validating the site.

Add deterministic Bun install/build checks and browser verification for navigation, search, code blocks, external links, raw Markdown, llms.txt, responsive layout and the unofficial-project notice. Check representative pages on desktop and mobile viewports.

Done when a clean checkout can install the pinned documentation dependencies and build/start the Fibel site, all documented commands match the CLI, browser checks pass without console errors, the disclaimer is visible and unambiguous, raw Markdown and discovery routes work, and no private domain, credential or organization-specific operational detail is present.
result: Built an isolated English Fibel site under docs-site with @valentinkolb/fibel pinned to 0.0.9 and Bun 1.3.14 lock metadata; the Go CLI remains independent of Bun. Added overview, installation, authentication/_FILE secret injection, production versus OT&E, DNS reads, preview/expect/apply mutations, JSON/exit codes, troubleshooting, security, and explicit limitations. The landing page has a prominent independence notice; every page carries an unambiguous footer notice linking to official INWX, while default Fibel attribution, search, theme, raw Markdown, and llms routes remain enabled. siteUrl is intentionally unset until a publication hostname is selected. Verification: a staged clean-checkout export completed frozen Bun install, 7 route/content/help-contract tests, and Fibel build; Go tests and credential scan passed. Real Chromium checks passed on desktop and 390x844 mobile for navigation, responsive menu, search/results, code blocks, theme controls, official/GitHub links, raw .md, llms.txt, and persistent notice with zero local console errors or warnings. No official logo, private domain, credential, PII, or organization-specific operational detail was added.

name: Create and evaluate the reusable INWX agent skill
description:
Create skills/inwx/SKILL.md as a concise generic operational skill for agents using the inwx binary. Trigger for INWX account inspection and DNS record work. Reference inwx --help for syntax rather than copying the complete CLI manual.

Require exact authorization for deletes and for NS, SOA, MX, DNSSEC or broad zone changes. Refuse fuzzy destructive matching and unrelated cleanup. name: Build the robust generic INWX CLI and agent skill
description:
Build and release a public, provider-specific command-line tool plus reusable agent skill in k2b-dev/inwx-cli. The executable is named inwx. The first release is deliberately DNS-focused, while the command hierarchy and internal boundaries must allow later INWX capabilities without renaming the binary or claiming unsupported functionality.

Product contract:
- Use Go and produce CGO-free standalone binaries. Prefer the maintained github.com/libdns/inwx provider for INWX JSON-RPC, record operations and TOTP support; write a thin direct API client only if a documented provider gap blocks a required contract.
- Keep runtime dependencies minimal. Use the Go standard library for command parsing, JSON, terminal tables and HTTP-adjacent behavior. Do not introduce Cobra, Viper, a database, a daemon or a plugin framework without a demonstrated requirement.
- Reserve top-level capability groups. The initial commands live under inwx dns ..., leaving room for future inwx domains ... or other explicitly designed groups. Do not implement domain registration, contacts, transfers, payments or account administration in v0.1.
- Provide stable human-readable output and an explicitly versioned machine-readable JSON mode for agents and scripts. Errors go to stderr, data goes to stdout, exit codes are documented and secrets are always redacted.

Initial command surface:
- inwx version
- inwx auth check
- inwx dns zones list
- inwx dns records list <zone>
- inwx dns records create <zone> ...
- inwx dns records update <zone> --id ...
- inwx dns records delete <zone> --id ...

Safety and authentication:
- Read credentials from INWX_USERNAME, INWX_PASSWORD, INWX_SHARED_SECRET and corresponding _FILE variables. Support an explicit production or OT&E endpoint. Never accept passwords or TOTP secrets as command-line flags, persist them in repository configuration, print them, or include them in debug output. Secret-manager integration remains external and generic; the public skill may explain environment injection but must not depend on fd0 or duplicate another secret-management skill.
- Read commands are non-interactive. Mutations first fetch the exact current state and display a deterministic proposed diff. The initial safety contract requires --apply to perform a mutation; delete additionally requires an exact record ID. Re-read the API after mutation and provide enough output for authoritative DNS verification. Never select a destructive target using a fuzzy name match.
- Preserve unrelated records and provider-managed fields. Define behavior for duplicate records, trailing dots, apex names, TTL bounds, priorities, TXT quoting, IDN normalization, pagination, retries, timeouts, rate limits and interrupted requests before claiming robustness. Do not present separate API calls as transactional.

Scope boundaries:
- v0.1 manages individual DNS records and lists zones. It is not a Terraform replacement and has no bulk YAML apply, hidden desired-state database, background reconciliation, ACME controller or DNSSEC mutation. These may be evaluated later as separate product work.
- Domain-management commands are future scope. The internal design should remain simple: add a new top-level command and service only when that capability is actually implemented; do not build speculative abstractions now.

Agent skill:
- Ship skills/inwx/SKILL.md in the same repository. It triggers for INWX inspection and DNS changes, uses JSON output for deterministic decisions, and follows read current state -> show exact diff -> obtain explicit authorization -> apply -> re-read -> verify authoritative DNS.
- The skill must prohibit casual NS, SOA, MX, DNSSEC and destructive changes unless the user explicitly requests the exact operation. It references CLI help rather than duplicating every flag and contains no organization-specific domains, credentials or infrastructure details.
- Add focused evaluation prompts for record inspection, a safe CNAME creation, an update conflict and a refused ambiguous deletion.

Quality and release:
- Test the command contract and formatting with Go tests and an httptest JSON-RPC fake. Add opt-in integration tests against INWX OT&E using unique disposable records with cleanup. No production mutation occurs during automated tests.
- CI runs formatting checks, go vet, tests, race tests where supported, vulnerability scanning and build/smoke tests for Linux and macOS on amd64 and arm64. Release immutable versioned binaries with SHA256 checksums and the bundled skill.
- Document installation, credential injection, OT&E use, JSON schema/exit codes, safety model, examples and limitations. Use MIT licensing.

The epic is complete when v0.1.0 is published, its checksums and clean-machine execution are verified, the skill has passed its focused evaluations, OT&E CRUD and cleanup are proven, no credential reaches Git/logs/process arguments, and a new agent can safely inspect and change an INWX DNS record using only the repository documentation and skill.

Brand and independence:
- Present the project everywhere as an unofficial community CLI. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, maintained by or supported by INWX GmbH. Link to the official INWX site for official services and support, and do not use official logos or visual branding in a way that implies affiliation. The disclaimer must be visible in the README, Fibel documentation site, installer help/output and release notes.

Documentation and installation deliverables:
- Build a dedicated public developer documentation site with @valentinkolb/fibel. Keep its Bun toolchain isolated from the Go CLI. The site must document installation, auth, OT&E, command behavior, JSON automation, safety and troubleshooting; expose normal Fibel search and machine-readable Markdown/llms routes; and pass local build plus browser verification. Production hosting and DNS are separate until a hostname is explicitly selected.
- Ship a POSIX installer/updater modeled on fd0.sh: Linux/macOS amd64/arm64, ~/.local/bin default, --system/--prefix/--version, downgrade protection, atomic replacement, SHA-256 validation and keyless Cosign verification bound to the exact k2b-dev/inwx-cli workflow/tag. It installs only inwx and never handles INWX credentials. Add isolated installer integration tests and document both convenience and release-pinned curl flows.
result:
Completed the INWX CLI v0.1 epic and published v0.1.0.

Delivered:
- A small CGO-free Go binary named inwx with versioned human/JSON output, redacted _FILE-based authentication, explicit production/OT&E selection, DNS zone/record reads, and exact-ID A/AAAA/CNAME/TXT/MX mutations under inwx dns only.
- Every mutation is a deterministic no-write preview followed by a fresh exact --expect token, explicit --apply, API re-read, and verified postcondition; unrelated records are preserved and unsupported registrar, NS/SOA, DNSSEC, bulk-state, and account capabilities remain out of scope.
- An isolated Fibel documentation site with search, raw Markdown/llms routes, browser tests, and persistent unofficial-community disclaimer. Hosting remains intentionally unconfigured pending a separate hostname/hosting decision.
- A reusable provider-generic INWX agent skill with six evaluations; final grading passed 22/22 assertions versus 12/22 baseline.
- A POSIX fd0-style installer for Linux/macOS amd64/arm64 with downgrade protection, atomic replacement, SHA-256, and exact-workflow/tag Cosign verification.
- Pinned CI and release automation covering formatting, vet, unit/race tests, vulnerabilities, full-history secrets, docs/browser tests, installer tests, and four native platform smokes.

Release proof:
- Exact release commit ff0b5b32fcd06a37d91aecf71903bddbb05613e4 passed CI run 30212702964 and release run 30212759294.
- Public v0.1.0 archives, checksums, certificate, signature, and Sigstore bundle were independently downloaded and verified; archive skill bytes match Git and version metadata matches the tag/commit.
- The public installer installed the signed release into an isolated prefix.
- The installed release binary completed guarded TXT create/update/delete against a unique OT&E zone; every operation was re-read and verified, then record and zone cleanup returned the account to zero zones. Production was never called.
- No credential is stored in Git, fixtures, arguments, or captured output.

Release: https://github.com/k2b-dev/inwx-cli/releases/tag/v0.1.0

name: Implement previewed and conflict-safe DNS mutations
description:
Implement inwx dns records create, update and delete on top of the proven read path. Every mutation fetches current state first, validates an exact target, emits a deterministic before/after diff and performs no write without --apply. Update and delete use the provider record ID plus precondition checks; ambiguous or stale state fails closed.

Normalize supported names and values consistently while preserving provider semantics. Cover A, AAAA, CNAME, TXT and MX first, including TTL and priority. Reject unsupported or malformed types rather than silently coercing them. Re-read after a successful mutation and report both API state and a clear authoritative-verification next step.

Test create/update/delete success, duplicate creation, stale update, ambiguous lookup, missing ID, protected/unsupported record behavior, interrupted requests, retry boundaries and idempotent recovery. Run opt-in OT&E CRUD with unique names and guaranteed cleanup; never point automated tests at production.

Done when all mutation and failure tests pass, OT&E CRUD leaves no test records behind, --apply is required and verified, exact conflicts are reported without side effects, unrelated zone records remain byte-for-byte semantically unchanged, and logs/output contain no credential material.
result: Implemented exact-ID DNS record create, update, and delete with canonical A/AAAA/CNAME/TXT/MX validation, deterministic before/after previews, SHA-256 expect tokens, constant-time stale checks, mandatory --apply, non-retried single writes, full-zone re-read verification, protected-type refusal, CNAME/duplicate conflict detection, and idempotent lost-response recovery. Added value file/stdin inputs, stable human/JSON output, opt-in OT&E-only CRUD coverage, and operator documentation. Verification: go test ./..., go test -race ./..., go vet ./..., CGO-free darwin/linux amd64/arm64 builds, credential scan clean. A unique disposable OT&E zone ran preview/apply create-update-delete successfully; every state was re-read, record cleanup succeeded, the zone was previewed/applied for deletion, and a final list verified zero leftover zones. Production was never called.

name: Build the verified fd0-style installer
description:
Add a portable POSIX sh installer/updater for the inwx binary, modeled on the verified fd0.sh client-install flow without copying fd0-specific products, flavors or configuration behavior. The script installs only the CLI and never asks for, stores or migrates INWX credentials.

Support Linux and macOS on amd64 and arm64. Install to ~/.local/bin by default and support --system, --prefix=DIR, --version=vX.Y.Z, --allow-downgrade, --yes and --help. Resolve the latest stable CLI release when no version is given, detect an existing inwx binary, show current to target version, require confirmation for install/upgrade, preserve an existing binary on failure and print a PATH hint when needed. Running the installer again is the update path; do not add an inwx update command in v0.1.

Release archives use deterministic names such as inwx_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz and contain the inwx binary plus required notices. Download to a private temporary directory, validate the selected archive against checksums.txt, and verify the checksum manifest with keyless Cosign identity bound to the exact k2b-dev/inwx-cli release workflow, repository and tag. Refuse missing, malformed, mismatched or unverifiable artifacts. Prevent implicit downgrade when resolving latest and require --allow-downgrade for an explicit older version.

Keep release/API bases and verifier path overridable only through documented test environment variables. Quote all paths, reject malformed version/prefix values, avoid eval, clean temporary files with traps and use atomic replacement with correct executable permissions. Require sudo only for --system.

Provide isolated integration tests with temporary HOME/PATH and a local fake release server. Cover clean install, upgrade, same version, explicit version, downgrade refusal/approval, checksum mismatch, signature failure, unsupported OS/architecture, interrupted download, custom prefix and preservation of the previous binary.

Document a canonical curl installation command and a release-tag-pinned alternative. The final convenience URL may be selected with documentation hosting; do not invent a production hostname. State clearly that this is an unofficial community installer unrelated to INWX GmbH.

Done when shell lint and isolated integration tests pass, release candidates install and upgrade on all supported CI targets, every tampered or unverifiable artifact is refused, failed upgrades retain the prior binary, the installer contains no credential path, and the documented one-line command behaves exactly as described.
result: Added a POSIX sh installer/updater for the inwx binary only. It supports Linux/macOS amd64/arm64, ~/.local/bin, --system, absolute --prefix, exact stable --version, --allow-downgrade, --yes and help; latest resolution cannot downgrade. It detects and reports an existing version, refuses unknown binaries, confirms changes, downloads to a private temporary directory, authenticates checksums.txt with keyless Cosign bound to the exact k2b-dev/inwx-cli release.yml tag identity and GitHub OIDC issuer, validates strict SHA-256 entries, requires inwx plus LICENSE, smoke-checks the embedded version, and replaces atomically only after all verification succeeds. Failure leaves an existing binary unchanged; no credential path exists in the installer. Added exact canonical and v0.1.0-pinned raw-GitHub curl commands to README and Fibel docs, with Cosign and unofficial-project guidance. Isolated local HTTP/fake-Cosign integration tests cover four platform pairs, clean install, upgrade, idempotent same version, explicit version, downgrade refusal/approval, latest downgrade refusal, checksum/manifest/signature/download failures, unsupported platform, invalid input, unknown existing binary, custom prefix/PATH hint and exact identity binding. Verification: sh -n, Shellcheck, installer tests, go test, race, vet, Fibel tests/build and diff checks passed. Commit aee1daa pushed to origin/main.

name: Tolerate non-canonical INWX data on reads
description: Fix production read failures caused by provider-returned data that violates strict mutation-input validation.
